headline.label: Did tone lead decisions?
headline.detail: Interim, word-list scores: Out of sample, adding tone to the previous decision changed log loss by +0.004 per meeting (95% CI -0.030 to +0.036; above zero = better) and called 4 of 44 rate changes, against 0.

headline.label: Did gilts listen?
headline.detail: Interim, word-list scores: 2-year gilt move per point of speech stance on 648 speech days (95% CI -0.86 to +0.43 bp).

headline.label: How good is the AI?
headline.detail: Rank agreement with 33 hand labels by one student (95% CI 0.01 to 0.68); two different AI models agree with each other far more.

event_study.takeaway: Interim, word-list scores. Tone in the 12 weeks before hikes averaged +0.43, against -0.23 before cuts and -0.21 before holds (hike minus cut +0.65, 95% CI +0.52 to +0.79). Tone before hikes stood out, while holds and cuts looked alike; tone did not visibly build up in the final weeks before a move.
event_study.method: Mean stance of MPC-relevant speeches and minutes published in each week before the announcement (week 0 = the 7 days before it; the decision's own minutes never count); 95% bands by bootstrap over decisions.

prediction_test.takeaway: Interim, word-list scores. Adding tone to the previous decision did not reliably improve out-of-sample forecasts (log-loss gain +0.004, 95% CI -0.030 to +0.036). Once the 2-year gilt yield is in the model, which on its own forecasts far better, tone adds nothing reliable (gain +0.025, CI -0.027 to +0.079).
prediction_test.method: Ordered logit, expanding window: before each scheduled decision from 2003 the model is re-fitted on earlier decisions only, with tone from documents published before each announcement. Accuracy is out of sample; pseudo R² is in sample.

coefficients.label: Change in tone vs previous window

market_reaction.takeaway: Interim, word-list scores. On 648 speech days, a one-point more hawkish speech went with a -0.21 bp move in the 2-year gilt (95% CI -0.86 to +0.43, p = 0.52); random non-speech days produce slopes this large 32% of the time, so this is a null result.
market_reaction.measure: Average absolute daily change in the 2-year gilt yield
market_reaction.method: Close-to-close change on the business day a speech was published; MPC announcement and minutes days excluded. Newey-West standard errors.

regression.label: Stance surprise vs last 60 days (bp per point)

caveats.title: Interim: word-list scores
caveats.text: These results use the word-list baseline, not the AI scorer: the AI pass over the full corpus has not run yet. The baseline agreed with the hand labels about as well as the AI did, but it is a cruder reading of tone. Every number here will be recomputed from the AI scores.

caveats.title: A small sample
caveats.text: About 315 decisions, only about 70 of them rate changes, and 36 hand labels. Effects of a plausible size are hard to detect, so 'no evidence' is not 'no effect'.

caveats.title: One labeller
caveats.text: The AI was checked against one student's labels. The two AI models agree with each other far more than either agrees with him, so the labels are a noisy yardstick.

caveats.title: The model knows history
caveats.text: The language model was trained on text written after most of these speeches. Hiding the date and speaker reduces, but cannot remove, the risk that it recalls what happened next.

caveats.title: End-of-day yields
caveats.text: Gilt yields are daily closes and speech times are unknown, so a speech after the close shows up a day late, and other news on the same day (data releases) is not controlled for.

caveats.title: Correlation, not causation
caveats.text: Tone and decisions are both driven by the economic data. A link between them does not mean speeches caused the moves.
